outcome: Produce a construction model and layered reference package that matches the preferred grayscale quality and later scoped directions, then obtain Nick approval.
authorizedScope: Continue modeling, render/compare/audit loops and export preparation. Subscription generation only. No final art approval by agents; no production rigging, animation, lore or game changes.

criteria.expectation: A complete creature with consistently developed large and medium forms. Review the whole body and regional closeups together before presentation.
criteria.assessment: The head now carries coat masses front and back, but the body is smooth clay with muscle-like knots, so the two read as different finishes.

criteria.expectation: Reconstruct forehead, temples, cheeks and jaw as related volumes. Front and profile must retain a rounded, appealing head without copying the generated study's inward gaze.
criteria.assessment: Measured against figure height, the neck is about 40 percent and the shoulders and waist about 30 to 40 percent wider than the first sheet, which makes the head and ear fan read small. The lower face is broad with a flat chin.

criteria.expectation: Preserve the accepted large eyes while modeling curved eye volumes, surrounding lids and their transition into the skull. Match contour, relative white area and projection before adding gloss.
criteria.assessment: Eye shape is close to face study 0010, but the eyes stand proud of the face as disks in profile and three-quarter views.

criteria.expectation: Keep forward gaze. Separate geometric integration from later glossy material and catchlight treatment; neither can substitute for the other.
criteria.assessment: Forward, centered pupils with coherent highlights in 0156. Construction comparison only, not Nick approval.

criteria.expectation: Establish the shallow paired muzzle and chin in actual geometry. Readable projection is required in profile without enlarging it into a different animal's snout.
criteria.assessment: The nose reads as a dark triangle with a compact mouth from the front, but in profile it is still a small bead with a notch beneath it.

criteria.expectation: Form connected cheek and crown masses that change the silhouette naturally. Broad flow belongs to construction; individual hair strands can wait.
criteria.assessment: Independent review of 0156 finds cheek tufts and a crown crest present; they are thinner than the reference cheek flare.

criteria.expectation: Establish a continuous shaggy envelope with varied overlap, width, curvature and taper. Adding more copies of the same lobe will not resolve the material or silhouette.
criteria.assessment: Measured against figure height, the fan span matches the first sheet within about .02 at every height from 3 to 15 percent of the figure. It reads narrow because the torso is too broad. The top edge is flatter and the fan hangs slightly low around the cheeks.

criteria.expectation: A legible cupped tissue surface with soft, intentional rim transitions and coat rooted around it. A recess being opaque does not make its shape acceptable.
criteria.assessment: No cupped inner ear reads from the front, and in profile the cavity is a thin-walled open trough.

criteria.region: Ear depth, rear surfaces and roots
criteria.expectation: Solve ear thickness, rear coat volume and cranial attachment together in front, profile and rear oblique views. Removing a mesh seam is not the same as achieving a convincing attachment.
criteria.assessment: Rear coat 0152 replaced the bald dish with flowing locks parted at the midline, but the fan still reads as one continuous dish from behind with pinched lock tips, and the round head does not show between two wings.

criteria.expectation: Related neck, shoulder and upper-arm volumes with plausible soft transitions. The reference pose differs, so reproduce the mass relationships rather than tracing its arm outline.
criteria.assessment: Square, shelf-like shoulders wider than the hips; the neck is about 40 percent too wide.

criteria.expectation: Continuous large planes and volume transitions through chest, waist and pelvis, without circumferential bands. Check oblique light and profile, not only a front silhouette.
criteria.assessment: The trunk is a straight tube: the first sheet is pear-shaped with hips a little wider than shoulders; the model is the reverse.

criteria.expectation: Express upper-arm/forearm mass, elbow direction and wrist-to-paw transition while preserving compact animal extremities. Lowered arms should expose these forms, not excuse them.
criteria.assessment: Independent review of 0156 finds sensible arm length and readable wrists; the forearms bow slightly and a small upper-arm knot remains under C01.

criteria.expectation: Rebuild the paw's outer volume and digit grouping before claw detail. Show front, side and underside as needed; retain the absence of a human thumb.
criteria.assessment: From the side four digits read; from the front the paw is one bulb with two crossing claws, and the claws are small barbs under the toes rather than curved tip claws.

criteria.expectation: Integrate the extra bounding strength into hip/thigh/knee form. Modest fullness must not become a literal rabbit leg or isolated muscle balloon.
criteria.assessment: Heavy thighs with lumpy, slightly inturned knees.

criteria.expectation: Preserve the straight joint-to-joint shin while shaping its surrounding volume and calf taper. Judge the rendered contour and planes, not only the numerical centerline.
criteria.assessment: An inner mid-calf bulge makes the outline knobbly; the reference calf tapers smoothly.

criteria.expectation: Restore local joint structure, a believable change of direction and the reference's sloping paw roof. Avoid both a human heel and a featureless continuous arc.
criteria.assessment: The ankle narrows from the front, but in profile the heel is a vertical wall without an Achilles curve.

criteria.expectation: Build a substantial paw body behind the digits, integrated toes and clear ground contact. Toe bumps and claws cannot stand in for the entire foot.
criteria.assessment: Four toes with claws and planted contact, but the toes sit in a straight row, the claws lie on the toe fronts, and the paw is about 25 percent small relative to height (.094 against .12).

criteria.expectation: Retain three full tails and pointed ends while refining their three-dimensional cross-sections, curvature and taper. Do not rotate each tail for each camera to imitate incompatible generated views.
criteria.assessment: From behind the crescent sweep and upturned tips match study 0018; the deeper sweep improves the profile, but in profile and rear three-quarter the tails are still pods thickest near the tip.

criteria.expectation: Preserve the centered, body-level three-way fusion with no stalk or extra bulb; refine continuity into a restrained pelvis. Occlusion alone is not evidence that the root moved to the left.
criteria.assessment: Independent review of 0156 finds one smooth fused root on the lower back with clean blending; the opposite-side wall is a rounded overlap edge. Forearm clearance over the tail is checked under C12.

criteria.expectation: Develop controlled medium-scale planes and attachments. More triangles, global smoothing or fur cannot replace this work.
criteria.assessment: The body has no coat masses; its only secondary forms are muscle-like lumps.

findings.observation: The head now carries coat masses front and back, but the body is smooth clay with muscle-like knots, so the two read as different finishes.
findings.nextAction: Develop broad coat masses on the body and soften the arm and back knots before surface work.

findings.observation: Measured against figure height, the neck is about 40 percent and the shoulders and waist about 30 to 40 percent wider than the first sheet, which makes the head and ear fan read small. The lower face is broad with a flat chin.
findings.nextAction: Slim the neck and torso toward the first sheet widths (neck about .065, shoulders about .20, waist about .14 of figure height) without moving the accepted tail root, then recheck the head read.
findings.priorResolution: Rechecked in actual assembly 0063: 0052 retains a rounded reconstructed cranium and cheeks with a smaller head-to-body ratio. Front and profile improve over the rejected wedge-shaped 0020. Subjective likeness remains unapproved.

findings.observation: Eye shape is close to face study 0010, but the eyes stand proud of the face as disks in profile and three-quarter views.
findings.nextAction: Sink each globe into a socket, bring the rim flush and add brow and cheek mass over the edge; recheck in profile.

findings.observation: Forward-centered glossy ocular volumes retain balanced pupils without the earlier inward gaze. This is a construction comparison, not Nick approval.
findings.resolution: Forward, centered pupils with coherent highlights in 0156. Construction comparison only, not Nick approval.

findings.observation: The nose reads as a dark triangle with a compact mouth from the front, but in profile it is still a small bead with a notch beneath it.
findings.nextAction: Blend the nose underside into the upper lip and fill the notch; keep the front triangle.

findings.observation: The cheek fringe is acceptable; small forehead pits and nubs near the top center remain.
findings.resolution: Independent review of 0156 finds cheek tufts and a crown crest present; they are thinner than the reference cheek flare.

findings.observation: Measured against figure height, the fan span matches the first sheet within about .02 at every height from 3 to 15 percent of the figure. It reads narrow because the torso is too broad. The top edge is flatter and the fan hangs slightly low around the cheeks.
findings.nextAction: Do not widen the fan. Lift its lower outer edge about .02 of figure height, let the outer ends rise, and recheck after the torso is slimmed.

findings.observation: No cupped inner ear reads from the front, and in profile the cavity is a thin-walled open trough.
findings.nextAction: Carve a forward-facing cupped cavity with a thick rim so a triangle reads from the front, and make the profile cavity shallow.
findings.priorResolution: Rechecked in actual assembly 0063: The reconstructed ear has continuous cupped tissue and a rounded shared rim. Front and profile no longer expose the old beaded shell construction.

findings.observation: Rear coat 0152 replaced the bald dish with flowing locks parted at the midline, but the fan still reads as one continuous dish from behind with pinched lock tips, and the round head does not show between two wings.
findings.nextAction: Notch the fan above the skull so the round back of the head shows between two wings, use fewer larger clumps per wing and soften the pinched tips.

findings.observation: Square, shelf-like shoulders wider than the hips; the neck is about 40 percent too wide.
findings.nextAction: Slope and narrow the shoulders with the torso slimming and round the skull underside into a slimmer neck.
findings.priorResolution: 0077 front, profile and trunk closeups show a continuous neck and shoulder root without the former cutoff lip or shelf. Independent review retains this correction. Local inner-arm dents remain under C12.

findings.observation: The trunk is a straight tube: the first sheet is pear-shaped with hips a little wider than shoulders; the model is the reverse.
findings.nextAction: Narrow the chest and shoulders and let the hips read wider than the waist, without human-like rear forms.
findings.priorResolution: Rechecked in actual assembly 0063: Coarser local relaxation removes paired chest bulges and rounds the crotch transition while preserving a slender torso and restrained pelvis. No separate human-like rear forms were added.

findings.observation: Arm proportion is acceptable; the elbows lack a landmark and the forearm is nearly as thick as the paw. Forearm grooves were softened in 0141.
findings.resolution: Independent review of 0156 finds sensible arm length and readable wrists; the forearms bow slightly and a small upper-arm knot remains under C01.

findings.observation: From the side four digits read; from the front the paw is one bulb with two crossing claws, and the claws are small barbs under the toes rather than curved tip claws.
findings.nextAction: Reduce the dominant outer digit so all four read from the front and move the claws to the digit tips, curving toward the palm.

findings.observation: Heavy thighs with lumpy, slightly inturned knees.
findings.nextAction: Merge the knee and thigh bulges into one smooth transition while keeping the requested fullness.

findings.observation: An inner mid-calf bulge makes the outline knobbly; the reference calf tapers smoothly.
findings.nextAction: Merge the inner calf bulge into one taper from knee to ankle.
findings.priorResolution: 0077 profile places calf fullness posteriorly and no longer shows the earlier bowed mid-shaft tube. Independent review retains shin direction; knee and ankle findings remain separately open.

findings.observation: The ankle narrows from the front, but in profile the heel is a vertical wall without an Achilles curve.
findings.nextAction: Add an Achilles curve above the heel in profile.

findings.observation: Four toes with claws and planted contact, but the toes sit in a straight row, the claws lie on the toe fronts, and the paw is about 25 percent small relative to height (.094 against .12).
findings.nextAction: Arch the toe row, scale the paw up about 25 percent, and move the claws to the toe tips curving down.

findings.observation: From behind the crescent sweep and upturned tips match study 0018; the deeper sweep improves the profile, but in profile and rear three-quarter the tails are still pods thickest near the tip.
findings.nextAction: Move each tail's widest section from about 75 to about 50 percent of its length, reduce depth about 25 percent and taper into the crescent.

findings.observation: The opposite-side wall is now a rounded overlap edge, but the three roots meet in a narrow knot with a crease line rather than a thick fused root spreading over the rump.
findings.priorResolution: 0077 removes all old tail remnants and shows three full tails joining directly at a compact body-level root. All three authored root X values are zero with overlapping bases. Independent review confirms the centered fusion and restrained pelvis; tip quality remains open under C18.
findings.resolution: Independent review of 0156 finds one smooth fused root on the lower back with clean blending; the opposite-side wall is a rounded overlap edge. Forearm clearance over the tail is checked under C12.

findings.observation: The body has no coat masses; its only secondary forms are muscle-like lumps.
findings.nextAction: Bring torso, limbs and tails to the same medium-form development as the head before surface work.

audit.reviewer: Claude primary plus three independent Opus visual reviews (0139, 0149, 0156) and silhouette measurements
audit.comparison: Combined model 0156 adds rear coat head 0152 and deeper crescent tails body 0155 to the 0149 chain. The third review verified three tails and four toes. Height-normalized silhouette measurement shows the ear fan span matches the first sheet while the neck and torso are 30 to 40 percent too wide, so the fan reads narrow. Passes: C04, C06, C12, C19.
audit.regressions: Tail tips curl up per accepted study 0018 rather than droop as in the first sheet; reported to Nick as a visible shape decision. Preserve the central body-level three-tail fusion, forward gaze and animal-paw direction.
audit.scopeCheck: Continue the authorized correction loop. Torso and neck slimming is the next correction, then ear notch and inner cup, eye sockets, paws, legs and tail girth. Nick approval is not the blocker.
